decisions.statement: One page is left for every recording more than one page states the key of.
The page left is the one whose slug sorts first among the pages stating that key.
Slugs sort by the code point, so the same pages always leave the same one.
The page left is chosen as a sweep chooses the page a recording is filed under.
The page left states one carrier for every release any page in its group named.
Two pages naming one release give that release's carrier from the first of them.
The carriers are ordered by the release each one names.
The page left names every collection any page in its group named.
The collections that page already named come first, in the order it named them.
The page left is heard where any page in its group was heard.
A page left naming no song takes the song the first page in its group names.
Every other page in the group goes, with every file beside it.
A track stating no key is left alone and counted as skipped.
A recording one page alone states is left alone.
A page's slug is left as it is, though it names one of the releases carrying it.
Every page written and every page taken away lands as a single commit or not at all.
Nothing outside the pages taken away names those pages, so nothing is re-pointed.

definition: the command leaving one track page for a recording, whatever releases carry it
